text:
kim: Heads-up — scheduling deploy for feature/kv-cache today at 18:00 PT. Canary to 10% for 15m then ramp. Who's owning smoke + off-ramp?

devon: I can own the smoke checks and watch metrics. Will be available in the channel.

maria: I’ll be on standby for rollback steps and will coordinate the feature-flag flip if needed.

kim: Awesome. Runbook is here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/offramp-primer — please review before 17:45. Key checklist in that doc.

saul: Quick q: DB migration included?

devon: No DB schema changes; it’s KV cache only. No migrations.

release-bot: Deploy window reserved: 18:00–18:30 PT, owner: kim, canary 10%->50%->100% (automated ramp).

kim: Smoke items: 1) healthcheck /ready on all pods 2) p50/p95 latency on API <= baseline+15% 3) error-rate spike < 1% 4) artifacts present in S3.

maria: I’ll run a scripted smoke: 
```
./scripts/smoke_kv_cache.sh --target canary
# checks: /health, sample GET/SET workload, tail logs for exceptions
```

devon: Alert thresholds we’ll watch: p95 > 500ms OR errors > 1% sustained for 5m -> trigger rollback. Confirm?

kim: Confirmed. Also manual override: any senior oncall can call immediate rollback.

saul: Who flips the flag to disable? Is it LaunchDarkly?

maria: Yes, LD toggle: `kv_cache.enabled`. I have permissions. Will flip to false to cut feature.

ops-bot: Reminder: Canary telemetry dashboard at https://grafana.redwood/d/kv-cache-canary (auto-refresh 15s).

devon: On the undo plan — two-step: 1) disable flag 2) revert deployment if necessary. Revert command for k8s: 
```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/kv-cache-service --to-revision=$(kubectl -n prod rollout history deploy/kv-cache-service | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print $1}')
```

maria: Note: also clear local KV cache on edge nodes if errors persist: `curl -X POST https://ops.redwood/clear-cache` (auth required).

kim: Who will make the go/no-go call at canary -> ramp?

devon: I will make the go/no-go after 15m canary and report in channel.

saul: Quick permission check: kim, can we add emergency ssh access to oncall?

kim: Yes — security pre-approved for this window. Use the breakglass flow in the runbook.

maria: I’ve added the rollback snippet to the runbook section and preloaded the LD flag toggle.

devon: Preflight checklist I ran at 17:40: code review ✅, staging smoke ✅, infra health ✅, quotas OK ✅.

kim: Great. Final asks before 18:00?

saul: Can we get a short note to customer-success that deploy may affect latency for a few minutes?

kim: On it — pinged #customer-success with a heads-up.

release-bot: Deploy scheduled in 20 minutes. Auto-approve: false (manual start).

maria: I’ll post a short template for the rollback reason if we need it, so we can file the post-deploy notes quickly.

devon: Logging into the canary dashboard now. See you in the channel at 17:58 for handoff. :thumbsup:

kim: Thanks all — we’ll call the canary start at 18:00 PT. If you’re oncall and not here by 17:58, I’ll reach out.

ops-bot: Post-deploy reminder scheduled at 18:35 PT to gather observations and close the runbook.
